_comment: OF28: per-species shiny REPAINT rules, consumed by tools/repaint_creature_textures.py. Owner directive 2026-08-15: shinies are genuinely different colourways, never a tint -- 'if our newt is blue, I want red. not blue with a red shade over it. for the white and black striped badger maybe it becomes blue stripes.' Rules are HSV region remaps (first match wins per pixel); value/texture detail is preserved so the repaint reads as the same painted surface in a new colourway. All numbers tunable. Regenerate with: python3 tools/repaint_creature_textures.py
_comment_pilots: paddlenewt and burrowback are the owner's own named examples and the pilot pair; the rest of the roster gets colourways after the pilots pass a render judge.
_comment_selector: SELECTOR LESSON, learned three times in one round and written here so it is not learned a fourth. A colourway rule's `match` block selects on HUE, SATURATION and VALUE -- it cannot select on ANATOMY. Whenever the thing you want to recolour is a PART of the creature (ear tips, a face marking, veins, a crest), check first that some HSV band actually isolates that part in the SOURCE texture, by measuring it. Three times this round it did not, and each time the rule silently recoloured most of the animal instead: galewisp's `sat_min 0.16` gold gilded the whole bird because its source is uniformly hue 44; pipwing's `sat_min 0.30` face marking took 69% of the chick for the same reason; veridian's `sat_min 0.42` vein rule caught 87.9% of the stag. None of the three raised an error and all three looked plausible in the spec. If no HSV band isolates the part, the tool already has the right mechanism -- put it in `overlays`, which selects on real anatomy read out of the species' own glb (see `_comment_overlays`). Veridian is the one case where a band DID exist, just not the one first reached for: value, not saturation.

_finish_default._comment: CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23. Applied after every species' rules by tools/repaint_creature_textures.py, per-species overridable with a `finish` block ({} opts out entirely). These assets are photoreal-ish Meshy albedos: at the 40 pixels a wild creature actually occupies (shots/band3/09-wild-cluster-on-the-road.png) their fine detail is not fur, it is dithering, and the value gradients that carry a face on a 2048 map average to one flat tone. So: median-despeckle, quantise value into bounded zones, re-stamp the darkest 3% of the SOURCE so eyes/nostrils/outlines survive the smoothing, and downsample. All numbers tunable; the blind critique against docs/reference/palworld-0*.jpg is the gate, never these numbers.

_comment_terrain_key: CREATURE-PRESENTATION. The Meadows grass measures hue 134-155 / value 0.26-0.47 in shipped frames and the canopy hue 98. A wild species that stands in that band separates by value alone, which distance, shadow and overcast all take away -- so a body hue inside 80-175 degrees is a defect on any creature that walks on grass, and green is spent on ACCENTS (bramble sprigs, moss on plates, a legendary's crown) rather than on coats. The repaint tool prints the share of chromatic pixels each output leaves in that band.

paddlenewt._comment: Base: teal body, cream/tan belly plates, salmon accents, gold spots + eyes. Vivid (board: 'Vibrant blues + Wet sheen'): vibrant BLUE, not the first pass's emerald; the salmon and gold accents sit outside the band and keep their identity. Shiny: ember red, unchanged.
paddlenewt.vivid_comment: BRIGHT CYAN-TURQUOISE, per the board, and pushed further from ripplet's cobalt than the shipped 210 was: this is the light, tropical one of the three water species, and it needs to be readable as that at thumbnail size rather than as 'the middle blue'.

overlays._why: ONE ROSTER / surface rendering. Paddlenewt's scalloped belly plates are a high-contrast grid at texture resolution; on a 40-pixel creature they alias into fishnet. Pulling the belly's local contrast toward its own mean keeps the scallops as a surface and stops them ringing. A blur would smear at the same frequency; this reduces the amplitude instead.

burrowback._comment: Base: charcoal-black fur, off-white/cream stripe patches, grey stone plates. Vivid (board: 'Stone plates + Moss + Ancient'): the plates go COOLER and greyer and the moss goes heavier, because this species and terrapup are two different meshes of the SAME ARCHETYPE -- a badger-shaped quadruped at similar mass, which is why a blind round read them as one animal and mistakenly reported them as one mesh (they differ in vertex count, bounds and POSITION data; no two species here share a mesh file). Paint is therefore not powerless the way 'only geometry can' implied -- terrapup takes warm earth and heavy leaf, burrowback takes cold stone and moss. Shiny: REBUILT off cornflower blue. Both species' shinies were blue badgers with white face stripes and a blind round could not tell them apart; it went to pale marble over charcoal-violet -- and that collided with this same round's OTHER fix, which took the ORDINARY burrowback to cold grey stone. Two grey badgers; a blind round called the pair 'the same frame twice'. Moved again to warm bronze -- and a blind round measured THAT at value 0.24 against the ordinary's 0.28 and still called the pair 'the same frame twice'. Temperature was not enough because the values had converged. Third pass makes it a VALUE inversion: luminous pale bronze plates at high value over a body left near-black, so the rare is the bright-plated one and the ordinary the dark mossy one. A rare has to announce itself at 30% thumbnail size, and value is the only channel that survives that far.
burrowback.vivid_comment: Was: warm cream + mossed mid-tones, which read as the same warm animal terrapup already is on the same mesh. Now cold grey stone across all three bands -- the board's plates are grey rock, not warm hide, and cold-vs-warm is the strongest separation two creatures of one archetype can be given without touching geometry.

overlays._why: Board: 'Stone plates + Moss + Ancient', and the board's burrowback carries a LOT of moss between the plates -- the shipped 0.42 read as a moss strip rather than an old armoured animal, which a blind round named. Heavier, and reaching further down the flank, because the moss is the warm accent holding an otherwise entirely cold-grey creature together.

overlays_alpha._why: ALPHA PRESENCE. WILD-ECOLOGY already spawns a cluster leader bigger and stronger; it looked identical to its neighbours. Heavier, darker, higher-contrast stone across the back reads as armour at the distance where the size difference alone is ambiguous.
More of the same moss, and older: a leader has stood in one place long enough to grow a coat.

terrapup._comment: Base: amber/brown pup, mostly dark. Vivid (board: 'Warm earth tones + Moss accents'): warm earth, modest saturation, now carrying the board's real amount of leaf growth. Shiny: frost pup -- KEPT blue, and burrowback's shiny is the one that moved off the same cornflower, because the starter is the creature a player sees for the whole game and its rare variant is the one worth keeping memorable.

overlays._why: Board: the Ground starter is a PUPPY WEARING FOLIAGE -- leaf collar, shoulder growth and leaves carried well down the back. At coverage 0.45 over a y_min of 0.52 almost none of that survived into the render, which a blind round named ('leaf and bramble growth -- almost none of it survives'). Coverage up and the band reaches further down the flank, because this foliage is half of what separates the starter from burrowback -- which it does NOT share a mesh with, contrary to what round 2 reported and this lane was briefed: the two glbs differ in vertex count (15,616 vs 17,204), bounds and POSITION data, and no two species in the roster share a mesh file. They share an ARCHETYPE, a badger-shaped quadruped at similar mass, which is why they read alike at thumbnail size -- and that is a problem paint can genuinely work on, unlike the mesh-sharing version of the story. z_max still keeps it off the muzzle -- terrapup's head sits at the high-z end of its own box.

ripplet._comment: Base: bright teal water sprite. Vivid (board: 'Deep blues + Translucent fins'): the teal goes DEEP blue rather than brighter aqua. Shiny: sunset coral, unchanged.
ripplet.vivid_comment: COBALT BODY, CREAM UNDERSIDE. Two corrections in one. The board's ripplet is a two-tone animal -- blue over a white belly with pale inner ears -- and the previous pass rendered it as a single flat royal blue that a blind round read as a missing texture, noting its own SHINY proves the mesh supports two-tone blocking. The cause was `set_sat`: forcing one saturation onto 94% of the animal removes every variation the painted source had, which is exactly what makes a surface read as vinyl. `sat_scale` keeps that variation. The belly is selected on VALUE, measured rather than guessed -- 48% of this source sits above val 0.70 and that bright region is the underside.

galewisp._comment: Base: pale silver air starter. Vivid: the board's white + gold (see vivid_comment). Shiny: storm violet, now genuinely distinct because the ordinary bird stopped being blue -- and carrying white lightning tips so the rare reads by pattern as well as hue.

overlays_shiny._why: The rare's pattern: white lightning tips on the distal wing, which the ordinary white-and-gold bird has nowhere to put. Without this the shiny was a flat hue rotation of the same silhouette.

galewisp.vivid_comment: WHITE BODY, GOLD TIPS -- and the gold moves from a colourway RULE to an anatomical OVERLAY, which is the actual correction. The board paints a white/silver starter with gold ear and wing tips; a rule matching on saturation cannot say 'tips', so it gilded every saturated texel and produced a bird soaked in yellow all over. A blind round read the result as the ordinary and the rare having swapped places, since the shiny still wore the board's white. Same lesson `_comment_overlays` already records for galecrest's round-1 patches: placement is anatomy, never a colour band.

overlays._why: The board's gold, where the board puts it: the outer ears and the spread of both wings. The first version used `lateral_min 0.55, y_min 0.55` and the tool reported it covering 1.9% of the surface -- a blind round then measured the whole bird at saturation 0.08, pure white, with the accent that gives it its identity absent. The predicate is widened to reach the wing spread rather than only its furthest tip. `tint` so every feather line in the value channel survives underneath. THE TOOL PRINTS EACH OVERLAY'S COVERAGE -- read it, an overlay under a few percent will not be visible.
A half-strength touch of the same gold on the crown, which is what ties the ear and wing tips together instead of leaving them as separate flags.

meadowhart._comment: Base: golden-tan deer. Vivid (board: 'Natural browns + Antlers'): tawny natural brown, restrained -- the burnished-gold pass read as a trophy, not an animal. Shiny: pale silver spirit-hart, unchanged.

overlays._why: Board: greened antler tips. TINT, not growth -- an antler's ridges and its bright tip all live in the value channel, so recolouring hue/saturation and leaving value alone keeps the antler an antler.
A few real leaf clumps caught in the rack on top of the tint, so the greening reads as growth rather than as paint.

tuskroot._comment: Base: dark earth-brown boar. Vivid (board: 'Deeper browns + Moss + Mature'; canon: must read as Mudsnout grown up, same colour logic): rich deep brown, darker value -- the amethyst pass broke the family line outright. Shiny: deep jade, unchanged (green against brown, clearly apart).
tuskroot.vivid_comment: CREATURE-PRESENTATION: still the deepest brown in the roster and still darker than Mudsnout, but 0.68 was an unreadable silhouette rather than a mature one

overlays._why: Board: 'Deeper browns + Moss + Mature'. Tuskroot is mudsnout grown up, so it wears the SAME moss in a heavier coat -- same hue, more of it, further down the shoulder.
The evolution's own name. A thin creep of the same growth up the legs, which reads as age at any distance where the mantle is still legible.

mosshell._comment: Base: green/yellow-green turtle. Vivid (board: 'Teal shell + Moss growth'; canon: primary read is WATER): the greens go teal, the yellow-greens stay moss -- the first pass pushed everything green, which is exactly the Grass read the canon forbids. Shiny: REBUILT. Hue 16 over this species' pale texels produced pink-white flesh with red seams, which a blind round read as 'an albino with bleeding joints -- raw/sickly rather than rare'. Warm BRONZE shell instead, with the pale regions taken down and warmed so they read as old polished plate rather than skin -- and the shell overlay replaced too, since a later round found the rare changing only its SKIN while the shell, which IS the creature, stayed identical. The hue move is total (teal 44% + yellow-green 15% -> zero, all warm) but the two variants still measured within 0.02 of each other in VALUE, and value is the channel that survives thumbnail size and overcast. So the rare also goes DARK: an old weathered bronze shell against the ordinary's bright teal, which is a value read as well as a hue one. Was: autumn ember, unchanged.

overlays_shiny._why: Replaces the ordinary's green shell moss rather than adding to it -- same `id`, so it stands in and inherits the seed. This is the fix for the specific finding that this species' rare changed only its SKIN while its dominant feature, the shell, stayed identical, which made the pair indistinguishable from behind. The shell is the creature; if the rare does not change the shell it has not changed. Autumn rust-gold growth over a bronze shell, against the ordinary's green over teal. DARK bronze, and `relief` cut from 0.60 to 0.34, because the first attempt at a value gap did not land: `grow` composites value as `cv*(1-relief) + ramp*relief`, so at relief 0.60 more than half the painted value comes from the overlay's own noise ramp and is INDEPENDENT of whatever the colourway rules did underneath. On this species the shell is the dominant surface, so the overlay was quietly resetting the darkening the rules had applied -- the measured gap moved 0.02 to 0.04 for a rule change that should have been large. Darkening the overlay's own colour and letting more source value through is what actually moves it.

mosshell.vivid_comment: CREATURE-PRESENTATION: teal shell kept, but the moss band goes warm ochre -- a water turtle whose second colour was grass-hue green was still half a Grass creature at distance

overlays._why: Board: 'Teal shell + Moss growth' -- moss ON STONE, the shell's own scutes showing through it. The shell is the up-facing top of the mesh; relief keeps the scute seams visible under the carpet.

brooktail._comment: Base: blue-grey otter. Vivid: dark chestnut with a bright cyan water tail (see vivid_comment -- owner directive took this species off blue). Shiny: violet, which still reads as the rare against a warm dark ordinary and is now the only place any blue-violet appears on this animal.
brooktail.vivid_comment:
DARK CHESTNUT BODY, BRIGHT WATER TAIL. Owner directive, 2026-08-23, shown the roster: 'you should repaint the otter to not be blue... just too many are that similar shade of blue.' That overrides the board on this species, and it is the right call -- the board paints brooktail deep blue, but it also paints ripplet, paddlenewt, reedwing, pipwing and galecrest with blue in them, and a board read one card at a time does not show what the roster looks like as a set. Four blues is a board; six is a smear.

Chestnut is the choice because it does the most work at once. The species keeps its DARK value slot, which is the thing the roster is shortest of and which the previous navy was carrying. It reads as a real otter, which this mesh is. And putting a warm body under the bright cyan `water_tail` overlay makes that tail the only cool note on the animal, so the board's actual signature -- a water swirl at the back of a dark creature -- reads HARDER than it did when the whole otter was already blue. The first chestnut pass overshot: a blind round measured the body at value 0.18, DARKER than the 0.24 backdrop it stands against, and called it a silhouette hole with no readable detail. This source is already dark on its own (only 50% of it sits above val 0.35), so it needed LIFTING, not the val_scale 0.6 it got. The correction then overshot the OTHER way -- val_scale 1.30 took it to 0.48, mid-value like most of the roster, which fixed the readability and spent the dark slot to do it. val_scale 1.00 is the interpolation between the two measured points (0.6 -> 0.18, 1.30 -> 0.48) and should land near 0.35: comfortably clear of the 0.24 backdrop and still the darkest warm creature on the sheet. Recorded as two misses because the useful lesson is that this species' source is dark enough that val_scale is doing almost all the work, so it is worth measuring rather than nudging. Deliberately deeper and redder than the roster's existing warm browns (terrapup's copper-amber, mudsnout's orange, trailpup, meadowhart, tuskroot): at this value it does not join that group either.

overlays._why: The board's signature on this species is a bright water-swirl TAIL. The swirl itself is geometry this mesh does not have, but the bright-tail-on-dark-animal read is colour, and after the owner's 2026-08-23 direction took the body off blue this overlay is the ONLY cool colour on the creature -- which is what the board was actually drawing. Low y, away from the centre line, so it lands on the tail rather than the hindquarters.

galecrest._comment: Base: rust red-orange raptor. Vivid (board: 'White + blue + Noble'): saturated rust becomes teal-blue feathering, pale rust bleaches white, and the crest goes GOLD the way the board draws it. Shiny: REBUILT as a storm-dark eagle. The previous shiny was a brighter rust, and a blind round called the rarity inverted -- 'the shiny is natural brown plumage while the normal is the exotic white-and-blue one; the rare looks more common than the common.' Swapping the two was rejected: the board defines the ORDINARY bird as the white-and-blue noble, so a swap would contradict the owner's own reference. Instead the RARE moves to the one reading that outranks a noble white bird -- near-black storm plumage with electric tips.
galecrest.vivid_comment: Teal rather than the old flat slate 215: the board's wing feathers are blue-GREEN, and teal is what separates this bird from pipwing's pale blue at thumbnail size.

overlays._why: Round 1 put slate-blue on galecrest as a colourway RULE, so the blue landed wherever the source texture happened to be rusty -- blotches that cross feather boundaries, which a blind critic named. This is the same blue placed anatomically instead: the distal third of both wings (lateral extremes, above the feet), TINTED so every quill line, barb shadow and specular edge in the value channel survives and the colour flows along the feathers.

The board draws this crest and the legs GOLD, not blue. The old overlay put the wing's own slate on the crest as well, which left the bird reading as one blue note and cost it the warm accent the board gives it. Gold is also the only warm on any bird in the roster once galewisp takes its own.

overlays_alpha._why: ALPHA PRESENCE: the same storm blue, darker and reaching further up the wing.

overlays_shiny._why: The rare's pattern against a near-black body: electric cyan on the distal wing. This is what makes the shiny outrank the ordinary noble bird instead of reading as a duller version of it.

duskhush._comment: Base: grey-teal nocturne. Vivid: the board's dark plum (see vivid_comment). Shiny: REBUILT -- was plum-magenta 305, which the corrected plum vivid collides with, and which was one of the seven-of-seventeen shinies that all landed on pink/coral ('rare = turn it pink' is a filter language, not a design language). The midnight-blue rebuild did not work either: a blind round measured it at value 0.23 against the plum ordinary's 0.25 and called it a sideways hue nudge between two dark equally-saturated colours, invisible at range. Inverted instead -- the rare is now a PALE GHOST owl, near-white with its frost barring reading as pattern on a light body, against a genuinely dark plum ordinary. That is the largest value gap available on this species, and it is safe from the roster's other pale birds on silhouette and size: pipwing is a 0.60 m chick and galewisp a 1.90 m starter, against this owl's 1.28 m.

overlays_shiny._why: Inverted with the body: now DARK slate barring on a pale ghost owl, where it used to be ice barring on a dark one. The pattern is the same anatomy either way; what changed is which half of it is the light one, and a pale bird with dark bars reads at a distance a dark bird with pale bars did not.
The facial disc picks the same ice up at half strength -- what ties the wing barring to the bird instead of leaving it as two pale flags.

duskhush.vivid_comment: CREATURE-IDENTITY-3: the board paints this owl DARK PLUM with a pale cream facial disc; the shipped vivid was indigo 250 with a x1.45 brightening on every low-saturation region, which bleached the whole bird to pale lavender -- a blind round named it directly against the board. The x1.45 is the actual bleach and is gone. Body goes to plum 291 and DOWN in value; the disc keeps its own brightening but warm and modest, so the face still reads without the body following it up. This is also the roster's only dark-value creature -- everything else is mid-value pastel, which is a measurable part of why the sheet reads flat.

pipwing._comment: Base: sunny yellow songbird. Vivid (board: 'Soft grays + Blue tips'): the body goes pale gray, the saturated markings go sky blue. CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23: the second most common creature in the chapter (140 field spawns) was a pale grey body under pale sky-blue tips -- two pastels a stop apart, which is the 'tiny pastel blob at distance' the critics named (shots/band3/02-riverwatch-rest.png). The scheme is unchanged; the CONTRAST inside it is not. Near-white body, deep saturated blue tips: one light shape with dark marks on it still reads at forty pixels, where two pastels do not. Shiny: the sunny yellow the vivid retires comes back saturated as a canary-gold rare -- the old sky-blue shiny would have sat next door to the new blue-tipped ordinary.
pipwing.vivid_comment:
CREAM BODY, PALE BLUE FACE -- and the blue is an anatomical OVERLAY, not a colourway rule, which is the actual correction here. The shipped vivid set hue 214 at 0.75 saturation and made this chick read as 'small blue bird' beside reedwing's 'slightly bigger blue bird', which a blind round named. The owner then directed (2026-08-23) that too much of the roster sits in one shade of blue.

The first correction pulled the blue rule's saturation down and assumed that left a cream bird with a blue marking. Measured, it did not: this species' source texture is uniformly hue 44 at every saturation level -- 87.8% of it sits above sat 0.20 and the mean hue is 43 at every threshold -- so there is no marking-versus-body split for a saturation rule to find, and `sat_min 0.30` simply recoloured 69% of the bird. It was still a blue bird, just a paler one.

So the body goes cream through the rules, and the blue is placed where a face marking actually is: high on the model, near the centre line. Exactly the lesson `_comment_overlays` already records -- placement is anatomy, never a colour band -- and the same fix galewisp's gold needed this round for the same reason.

overlays._why: The board's pale blue on this chick is a FACE and crest marking, and anatomy is the only thing that can say so -- the source texture has no saturation band that isolates it. High on the model and near the centre line; `tint` so the down and feather detail in the value channel survives underneath.
A half-strength touch on the distal wings, which is what stops the face marking reading as a hat.

reedwing._comment: Base: pale waterbird. Vivid: the board's deep-blue crane (see vivid_comment). Shiny: REBUILT off pink -- it was hue 335, one of the seven-of-seventeen shinies that all landed on pink/coral. It went to copper-gold, and a blind round then found that gold colliding with pipwing's own gold rare AND with galewisp's ordinary -- three yellow birds. Moved again, to WHITE-AND-CRIMSON: a pale bird with deep red flight feathers and a crimson crown, which nothing else in the roster wears, reads unmistakably rarer than the navy ordinary, and stays clear of both the blue cluster and the gold one.
reedwing.vivid_comment: CREATURE-IDENTITY-3: the board paints a deep-blue crane -- saturated navy wings, a white breast and a yellow beak. The shipped vivid mixed a warm 45 across the body with a 205 blue at only x1.4 saturation, which is the pale washed blue-grey a blind round read as 'a domestic duck'. The mesh is a duck and stays one (CLAUDE.md: no new creature meshes for the Meadows) -- but a saturated navy waterbird with a white breast is a different animal at thumbnail size from a pale grey-blue farmyard one, and that half is paint's to fix. Beak rule runs FIRST because first match wins per pixel and the beak is inside the body's own warm band.

bramblebun._comment: Base: brown rabbit, cream chest, green bramble growth. Vivid: the board's leafy rabbit. Shiny: REBUILT -- the old rule was `set_sat 0.06, val_scale 1.18` and nothing else, i.e. bleach the animal white. That is not a colourway, it is the absence of one, and it is why this shiny reads as a rendering fault rather than a rare. The first rebuild took it to a near-black coat with crimson bramble, and a blind round found that WORSE -- 'a drab grey wild rabbit with pink decals; it reads MORE common than the ordinary', because a dark wild rabbit is the most ordinary animal on the sheet. Inverted: a pale SILVER-WHITE coat carrying deep crimson bramble. White-on-red is the rarest-reading combination available that no other species holds, and against the ordinary's warm russet it separates on value, hue and temperature at once.

overlays_shiny._why: The rare's pattern: the ear sprigs and the back ruff turn deep crimson against a near-black coat, on the SAME predicates as the green ones so it reads as the same plant in a different season. Shares the ordinary variant's overlay id on purpose: an `overlays_shiny` entry reusing a base id REPLACES that base entry rather than stacking on it, and inherits its noise seed, so this growth lands on exactly the patches the green one does instead of the rare wearing both colours of foliage at once.

The back ruff turned with the ears. Shares the ordinary variant's overlay id on purpose: an `overlays_shiny` entry reusing a base id REPLACES that base entry rather than stacking on it, and inherits its noise seed, so this growth lands on exactly the patches the green one does instead of the rare wearing both colours of foliage at once.

bramblebun.vivid_comment: CREATURE-PRESENTATION: leaf-green COAT -> warm hazel coat, green kept as the bramble accent it was named for

overlays._why: Board: leaf-shaped green ears are bramblebun's single signature. The ear pair is the top fifth of the mesh at the lateral extremes -- y>0.80 with |x| off the centre line -- on every rig, which a UV rectangle could not say.
Board: the ruff of leaves across the back and haunches is one of this species' two signatures and 0.3 left barely a fleck of it. The ears (0.82 above) survived; the body growth did not.

mudsnout._comment: Embedded-texture species. Base: mud-brown snuffler. Vivid (board: 'Rich browns + Mud texture'): CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23 lifted this off the floor. `val_scale: 0.7` on the roster's MOST COMMON creature (164 of the ~900 field spawns across five bands) made a dark unlit lump whose measured value distance from the grass was 0.14 -- less than the shadow of a cloud -- and buried the snout and eye the model actually has. Same hue family, saturation pinned rather than scaled so the mud reads as earth instead of the previous pass's salmon, and the value now works FOR the read. Shiny: pulled to clear rose-pink with a saturation floor -- the old h348 sat next to the vivid's warm brown across the red wrap.
mudsnout.vivid_comment: CREATURE-PRESENTATION: the same rich earth, but at a value the meadow does not swallow

overlays._why: Board: mud-brown snuffler carrying moss across the shoulders and spine. Up-facing surfaces only (up_min) -- moss grows where rain sits, and a boar's flanks are vertical.

trailpup._comment: Base: grey-brown wolf pup. Vivid: warm coat under the board's leaf growth. Shiny: REBUILT -- was hue 6 at x1.6 saturation against a hue 22/35 ordinary, so the rare was a slightly redder version of the common and read as neither rare nor different. Now a charcoal coat carrying EMBER-orange growth where the ordinary carries green: same animal, inverted season, and a value read rather than a hue nudge.

overlays_shiny._why: The rare's pattern: the same anatomical growth the ordinary carries in green, burning orange against a charcoal coat. Placed on the SAME predicates as the green so it reads as the identical plant turned, not as a different decal. Shares the ordinary variant's overlay id on purpose: an `overlays_shiny` entry reusing a base id REPLACES that base entry rather than stacking on it, and inherits its noise seed, so this growth lands on exactly the patches the green one does instead of the rare wearing both colours of foliage at once.

The throat ruff turned with the rest of it. Shares the ordinary variant's overlay id on purpose: an `overlays_shiny` entry reusing a base id REPLACES that base entry rather than stacking on it, and inherits its noise seed, so this growth lands on exactly the patches the green one does instead of the rare wearing both colours of foliage at once.

trailpup.vivid_comment: BROWN-GREY WOLF PUP under green growth, per the board. The previous pass set hue 35 at sat_scale 1.2 across a source that is 72% above sat 0.30, which produced a bright yellow-cream animal at value 0.69 -- and a blind round pointed out the consequence: this species' SHINY, a dark red-brown, is the one that looks like the owner's painting, so ordinary and rare are inverted against the board. The ordinary comes down in value and saturation into the muted brown-grey the board draws, which also gives the green leaf growth something to read against.

overlays._why: Board: growth over the shoulders and down the flank, not a saddle patch. 0.52 over a y_min of 0.58 put it all on the spine, which is why a blind round found 'almost none' of the board's foliage in the render.

The board's signature on this species is a broad green RUFF at the throat and chest -- the one thing that separates a leafy wolf pup from an ordinary one at silhouette size. The saddle above never reached it because it sits forward of the shoulder, at high z.

veridian._comment: Embedded-texture species. Base: leaf green. Vivid (board: 'Verdant glow + Ancient + Sacred'). CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23 SPLIT the board's three words across the model instead of spending all three on one hue. The chapter's climax creature was a saturated green stag on a green meadow -- 45 degrees of hue from the grass and the worst-camouflaged animal in the roster on the one encounter the whole chapter builds toward. veridian.vivid_comment:
CHARCOAL HIDE, EMERALD VEINS -- and the vein rule keys on VALUE, not saturation, which is the correction that finally made it land. The board paints the legendary as a near-black animal lit from inside. Two attempts failed before this one: the shipped vivid took the hide to val_scale 1.32 and a blind round measured a 'uniformly bright jade deer' that reads 'green deer, not legendary', and the first fix here darkened the wrong half, because it split veins from hide on `sat_min 0.42` and this source texture is 87.9% above that threshold. Rule one caught the whole animal and made all of it bright emerald.

Measured on the source: saturation cannot separate anything here (96.2% sits above sat 0.30), but VALUE can -- only 13.3% is above val 0.75 and 20.5% above 0.65, and that bright minority is the vein and glow work. So the veins are selected by `val_min` and everything else goes near-black.

THIRD TIME THIS ROUND a saturation-keyed rule failed to isolate a feature -- galewisp's gold tips and pipwing's face marking failed identically, each recolouring most of the animal instead of the part named. See `_comment_selector` at the top of this file.

overlays._why: LEGENDARY AT 100m. VERIDIAN-HIDE keeps the ivory hide -- this does not touch its hue. It deepens the underside so the stag carries a real value range instead of one flat pale mass, which is what a silhouette needs to survive against lit grass at distance.

overlays_emissive._why: The crown is the only part of this animal that is allowed to be green (VERIDIAN-HIDE), so it is also the part that has to carry the read at range. Boosted in the EMISSIVE map only: emission is the one channel distance, shadow and overcast do not take away, so a hundred metres out the player sees a pale stag with a burning green rack rather than a pale shape.
The other half of the same separation: the hide's own glow pulled DOWN, so the crown is the brightest thing on the model rather than one bright thing among many.

_comment_overlays: CREATURE-IDENTITY-2 2026-08-23. `overlays` is the board's FANTASY LAYER -- leaf ears, moss carpets, greened antler tips, storm-blue feather tips -- painted onto the existing UVs by tools/creature_overlays.py after the colourway rules and the finish pass. Round 1 delivered the palette and none of this, which a blind critic called 'correct but half-depth'. Every overlay is authored in ANATOMY (normalised height, surface normal, distance off the centre line, read out of the species' own glb by tools/creature_anatomy_maps.py), never in UV rectangles: an automatic unwrap scatters a wing across islands, so a rectangle that looks like a wing tip on the sheet is several unrelated pieces of bird -- that is exactly how round 1's galecrest patches ended up crossing feather boundaries. `overlays` applies to every colourway; `overlays_alpha` adds the cluster-leader variant, `overlays_emissive` the glow-only pass. No mesh is touched by any of this; mesh-level flourishes are in ralph/BLOCKED.md as an owner decision.
_comment_feature_key: CREATURE-IDENTITY-2: the per-species `finish.feature_max_val` numbers below are MEASURED, not chosen -- the value of the darkest 2.5% of each species' own SURFACE texels (the anatomy map's valid mask, so UV gutter does not vote). The shared 0.22 cap this replaced is the numeric form of the two-families problem: ripplet's darkest 2.5% sits at 0.384 and galewisp's at 0.314, both above the cap, so those two received NO feature re-stamp at all while burrowback (0.043) received a full one. That is why the chibi half of the roster reads soft-focus and glassy next to the naturalists. Measuring per species makes every creature re-stamp the same SHARE of its surface to the same shared dark, which is the one-roster eye/outline language at the level texture work can actually reach.
